prompt: Which section is the only one a CloudFormation template must have?
hint: Without it there is nothing to create.

choices.text: Parameters
choices.why: Parameters are optional; many templates have none.

choices.text: Resources
choices.why: Right. A template with no resources describes nothing to make.

choices.text: Outputs
choices.why: Outputs publish values and are optional.

choices.text: Conditions
choices.why: Conditions are optional, used to create a resource or not.

prompt: cfn-lint reports W3011 on a bucket with `DeletionPolicy: Retain`. What is still unprotected?
hint: Deleting a stack is one way to lose a resource; there is another.

choices.text: The bucket's objects, which Retain never covers
choices.why: Retain keeps the bucket with its objects; the gap is a different event.

choices.text: An update that replaces the bucket
choices.why: Right. Replacement deletes the old resource unless UpdateReplacePolicy is Retain too.

choices.text: Deleting the stack from the console instead of the CLI
choices.why: The policy applies however the delete is asked for.

choices.text: Turning on versioning later
choices.why: Versioning changes in place and threatens nothing.

prompt: Why run cfn-lint in the build, before `aws cloudformation deploy`?
hint: Compare where each one finds the mistake.

choices.text: Because CloudFormation does not validate templates at all
choices.why: It does, at the moment the stack is created or updated, which is the problem.

choices.text: Because cfn-lint deploys faster than CloudFormation
choices.why: cfn-lint deploys nothing; it only reads the file.

choices.text: Because AWS charges for every template it validates
choices.why: Validation is not billed; the cost of a late error is time and a rolled-back stack.

choices.text: A mistake becomes a failed build, not a stack that failed and rolled back
choices.why: Right. Found on the laptop or in the build, the mistake touches nothing in AWS.

prompt: To get the ARN of the resource `Uploads` inside a template, you write `!___ Uploads.Arn`.
hint: An intrinsic function that gets one attribute.

prompt: Where does CloudFormation keep the link between the logical id `WebLogs` and the log group `/shop/web`?
hint: Terraform needs a file for this; CloudFormation does not.

choices.text: In a state file the CLI writes beside the template
choices.why: CloudFormation has no state file; that is Terraform's arrangement.

choices.text: In the stack, readable with describe-stack-resources
choices.why: Right. The stack holds logical and physical ids side by side.

choices.text: In a tag on the log group
choices.why: CloudFormation adds tags, but the stack is the record it trusts.

choices.text: Nowhere: it looks the resource up by name each time
choices.why: Many resources have no name to look up; the stack records ids.

prompt: A stack's creation fails on its fourth resource. What state is the stack in afterwards, by default?

choices.text: ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, which only deletion gets out of
choices.why: Right. The three resources are deleted, and the stack can only be deleted and created again.

choices.text: CREATE_FAILED, with three resources kept for the next attempt
choices.why: Keeping the partial work is Terraform's habit, or DO_NOTHING's; the default rolls back.

choices.text: UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, ready to update
choices.why: That state follows a failed update, not a failed creation.

choices.text: DELETE_COMPLETE, gone as if never created
choices.why: The stack stays, in a rolled-back state, so its events can be read.

prompt: The lab deleted the stack `shop-base`. Why was the bucket still listed afterwards?
hint: Look at the bucket's policies in the template.

choices.text: moto never deletes buckets
choices.why: The log group from the same stack was deleted; the bucket was kept on purpose.

choices.text: A bucket with versioning cannot be deleted at all
choices.why: A versioned bucket can be deleted once empty; versioning was not the reason.

choices.text: Deleting a stack keeps every resource for 30 days
choices.why: No such grace period exists; the log group went at once.

choices.text: Its DeletionPolicy is Retain
choices.why: Right. Retain keeps the resource when the stack goes.

prompt: In a change set, which value of `Replacement` should make you stop and explain it before executing?
hint: Which one deletes a resource and makes a new one?

choices.text: False
choices.why: False means the resource changes in place.

choices.text: True, and Conditional read as True
choices.why: Right. Both may delete the resource and create a new one.

choices.text: None
choices.why: A real change set says True, False or Conditional; None is moto's.

choices.text: Import
choices.why: Import is an Action, not a value of Replacement.

prompt: A change set raises a log group's retention from 14 to 30 days and renames the uploads bucket. Which line will say `Replacement: True`?

choices.text: The log group's, because its retention doubles
choices.why: Retention changes in place; the log group stays the same one.

choices.text: Both, because any change to a stack replaces its resources
choices.why: Most properties change in place; replacement is the exception to look for.

choices.text: The bucket's: a new name means a new bucket
choices.why: Right. A bucket's name is its identity; renaming creates another one.

choices.text: Neither, because CloudFormation never replaces a bucket
choices.why: It does when the name changes, and deletes the old one unless told to retain it.

prompt: moto listed `Add` for all three resources in a change set on an existing stack. What does that tell you?
hint: What would AWS have computed for a parameter change?

choices.text: Nothing about AWS: moto computes change sets as if the stack were empty
choices.why: Right. On AWS this change would be one line, Modify WebLogs False.

choices.text: That the update would recreate the stack
choices.why: moto computes every change set as if the stack were empty; it says nothing about AWS.

choices.text: That the parameter was not passed
choices.why: The parameter was passed; the answer would be the same without it.

choices.text: That the stack had drifted
choices.why: Drift is a different comparison, and nothing had changed yet.

prompt: Put the steps of updating a production stack in order.
items: Edit the template and run cfn-lint
A person reads Action and Replacement
trap: Executing before reading is the slip: update-stack does exactly that.

prompt: Somebody changed a log group's retention in the console. The stack's template still says 14 days. What is that called?
hint: The resource moved away from the stack.

choices.text: A rollback
choices.why: A rollback undoes a failed change; nothing failed here.

choices.text: A replacement
choices.why: Nothing was replaced; the same log group has another value.

choices.text: A change set
choices.why: A change set is computed from a template, before a change.

choices.text: Drift
choices.why: Right. Drift is the resource differing from what the stack expects.

prompt: Which statuses can drift detection report for a resource? Choose all that apply.
hint: Four of them, one meaning it was not compared.

choices.text: IN_SYNC
choices.why: Yes. It matches what the stack expects.

choices.text: MODIFIED
choices.why: Yes. At least one property differs.

choices.text: REPLACED
choices.why: No. Replacement is a change-set word, not a drift status.

choices.text: NOT_CHECKED
choices.why: Yes. The resource type does not support detection.

choices.text: ROLLED_BACK
choices.why: No. That belongs to stacks, not to drift.

prompt: The change made at 2 a.m. was right: one day of logs is what the team wants now. What closes the drift properly?

choices.text: Leave it: the resource is already right
choices.why: The next update would put 14 back, undoing the fix at a random moment.

choices.text: Change the template to match, review it, update the stack
choices.why: Right. The fix is written down, and the stack and the resource agree again.

choices.text: Update the stack with the current template
choices.why: That restores 14 days, the value the team no longer wants.

choices.text: Delete the log group so the stack recreates it
choices.why: It loses the logs and recreates the old value.

prompt: Match each CloudFormation feature to the question it answers.

pairs.right: Is this file valid before AWS sees it?
What changed that nobody wrote down?

prompt: A pipeline should update a CloudFormation stack only after a person has seen what will change. How is that built?
hint: Two CloudFormation actions with something between them.

choices.text: One action running update-stack, then a manual approval
choices.why: The approval would come after the change was made.

choices.text: Run detect-stack-drift and approve if it is IN_SYNC
choices.why: Drift says what already changed, not what the update will change.

choices.text: Create a change set, approve manually, then execute it
choices.why: Right. CHANGE_SET_REPLACE, an approval, then CHANGE_SET_EXECUTE.

choices.text: Deploy to a copy of the stack first and compare
choices.why: A copy can help, but the change set is what shows this stack's changes.
